issues.legal_issue: Property allotted to a husband at partition and later possessed by his widow with a right to its income for her maintenance becomes her full property when she has a pre-existing right to maintenance.
material_facts: A family partition allotted the disputed property to the husband and allotted separate properties to the children.
The partition arrangement allowed the wife to reside in the property and, after her husband's death, to take its income.
After her husband's death, the widow exclusively possessed the property and used its income for her maintenance.
The widow's right to maintenance arose from her husband's personal obligation to maintain her.
issues.conclusion: The widow's possession and maintenance rights brought the property within Section 14(1) of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, and she held it as full owner.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14(1) applies to property possessed by a female Hindu and includes property acquired in lieu of maintenance. A Hindu woman's right to maintenance is a tangible, pre-existing right against property, and a husband has a personal obligation to maintain his wife. When she is placed in exclusive possession of property with a right to its income for maintenance, the property is presumed to have been given in lieu of maintenance; no express statement to that effect is required. Section 14(1) is to be construed liberally. The Court relied on V. Tulsamma v. Sesha Reddi and Gulwant Kaur v. Mohinder Singh, and treated Bai Vajia v. Thakorbhai Chelabhai as consistent with that principle.

predicates.female_property_succession_dispute: The proceeding concerns the ownership of property possessed by a female Hindu after her husband's death.
predicates.property_allotted_to_husband_at_partitio: The disputed property was allotted to the husband in a family partition.
predicates.widow_exclusively_possessed_property: After her husband's death, the widow was in exclusive possession of the disputed property.
predicates.widow_entitled_to_income_for_maintenance: The widow had a right to use income from the property for her maintenance.
predicates.widow_had_preexisting_maintenance_right: The widow had a right to maintenance arising from her husband's personal obligation to maintain her.

issues.definition: When a property-succession dispute involves property allotted to a husband at partition and exclusively possessed by his widow with income for her maintenance under her pre-existing maintenance right, the widow holds the property as full owner.

issues.legal_issue: The restriction on enlargement of a female Hindu's property interest does not apply when an instrument recognizes her pre-existing maintenance right rather than creating a new, restricted title.
material_facts: The partition arrangement allowed the widow to reside in the disputed property and take its income after her husband's death, while limiting the successors' ability to interfere with her enjoyment.
The property had been allotted to her husband at partition, and the widow possessed it with a right to income for her maintenance after his death.
The widow's maintenance right pre-existed the arrangement because her husband had a personal obligation to maintain her.
issues.conclusion: Section 14(2) did not prevent the widow's interest from becoming full ownership under Section 14(1), because her possession was traceable to her pre-existing maintenance right.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14(2) is an exception to Section 14(1) and applies where an instrument or other specified source creates a restricted interest in property. It does not displace Section 14(1) when property is acquired in recognition of an antecedent right, such as a right to maintenance. The Court relied on V. Tulsamma v. Sesha Reddi and Gulwant Kaur v. Mohinder Singh, and held that Bai Vajia v. Thakorbhai Chelabhai did not establish a different rule.

predicates.female_property_succession_dispute: The proceeding concerns the ownership of property possessed by a female Hindu after her husband's death.
predicates.widow_possession_traceable_to_preexistin: The widow's possession of the property was traceable to a maintenance right she already had.
predicates.instrument_recognized_maintenance_right: An instrument placed the widow in possession in recognition of her maintenance right.
predicates.instrument_limited_widow_to_residence_or: The instrument confined the widow's stated enjoyment of the property to residence or its income.

issues.definition: When an instrument limits a widow's stated enjoyment but recognizes a pre-existing maintenance right that explains her possession, those terms do not prevent her from holding the property as full owner.
